title: Faulty Keyboard
summary: Given a string s, simulate typing each character on a keyboard that reverses the string whenever an 'i' is typed.
statement: Given a string s, simulate typing each character on a keyboard that reverses the string whenever an 'i' is typed. Return the final string displayed.
constraints: Process the typed characters from left to right.
Typing i reverses all text currently on the screen and does not insert i.
Every other lowercase letter is appended; return the final screen text.
hints: Repeated physical reversal can be represented by one orientation flag.
Use a deque so a normal character is added to the logical end in either orientation.
Toggle the flag for i; append right normally and left when reversed, then orient once at the end.
The deque plus flag always represents exactly the visible text, so each typed character preserves the simulation invariant.
editorial: The deque plus flag always represents exactly the visible text, so each typed character preserves the simulation invariant.

tests.explanation: Typing i reverses str to rts, then n and g are appended, producing rtsng.
The two consecutive i keys reverse twice, so the final text is ponter.
